Fix entireio/entire-graph issue #350: Julia signatures include the whole body, and `module` symbols (Julia and Ruby) get false DATA_FLOWS edges.

Follow AGENTS.md and .entire/agent-guide.md. Use `entire graph query/def/neighbors/impact --head` for every locate or relationship question, and grep only for literal strings. Create a new branch `fix/julia-signature-module-dataflow` from an up-to-date main. Commit when you are done, but do NOT push; I will push and open the PR myself.

## Before changing code

1. Read the issue with `gh issue view 350 -R entireio/entire-graph`.
2. Build a "before" binary from the unchanged code: `go build -o /tmp/eg-before ./cmd/entire-graph`.
3. Recreate the issue's repro in a temp git repo: `src/Shapes.jl` and `lib/util.rb`, two commits, with the second commit a body-only edit. Run the issue's `snapshot`/`jq`/`diff` commands with /tmp/eg-before and keep the output for the PR.

## Part A: signatures (internal/sem/parser.go)

`signatureFromNode` (~8109) ends a signature at a `body` field or a body-like child. tree-sitter-julia keeps body statements as direct, unlabeled children, so nothing gets cut.

- Add `juliaSignature(node, src) string`, modelled on `fsharpSignature` (~4680).
- Apply it the same way the F# override is applied after entity construction (~6488), including recomputing `Fingerprint`.
- Check every Julia-gated case in the extraction switch (~5955-6060) for any path that sets `Signature` separately.

Cut rules. Confirm the node shapes by dumping the tree for a sample file rather than guessing:

- `function_definition` / `macro_definition`: end of the `signature` child. This keeps `::ReturnType` and `where {...}`, which sit inside `signature`. Expected: `function area(c::Circle)::Float64`, `function bump!(n)`, `function Base.show(io::IO, x)`, `macro trace(ex)`.
- `struct_definition`: end of `type_head`. Expected: `struct Circle <: Shape`, `mutable struct Counter`, `struct Point{T}`.
- `abstract_definition` / `primitive_definition`: keep the header whole, e.g. `abstract type A <: B end`.
- `module_definition` (including `baremodule`): end of the name. Expected: `module Shapes`.
- Short-form `assignment` (`f(x) = expr`, `f(x)::T = expr`, `f(x) where T = expr`): end of the left-hand side.
- If the expected child is missing, fall back to `signatureFromNode`.

Symbol IDs are `repo:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`; the signature is not part of them. Do NOT bump `IdentityRevision`. Prove the IDs are unchanged: collect the Julia symbol IDs from the before and after binaries on the repro and on `internal/sem/testdata`, and check the sets match.

## Part B: module DATA_FLOWS (internal/sem/provider.go)

`forEachRelation` sets `callableSymbol := !typeLikeKind(from.Kind)` (~5975). `module` is not type-like, so the DATA_FLOWS pass (~6024, which calls `returnFlowCalls` in types.go ~1052) scans a module's block. That block spans the module's member functions: the Julia `exactSymbolSource`, or the Ruby line span.

- Skip DATA_FLOWS when `from.Kind == "module"`, for every language. No language can `return` from a module body. Also make sure no DATA_FLOWS record has a module `to_id` through another producer.
- Keep the change local to the DATA_FLOWS gate. Do not change `callableSymbol` itself: it also gates ASYNC_CALLS (~5984) and the HTTP scan (~6176). List those in the PR as a follow-up.

## Part C: caches, tests, docs

**Cache versions.** Output changes for unchanged trees, and every local build shares provider version "dev". Bump both:

- `searchSnapshotCacheVersion` in internal/sem/search_cache.go: v25 to v26
- `providerRecordsCacheVersion` in internal/sem/records_cache.go: v19 to v20

Add a one-line comment to each in the existing "vNN retires ..." style.

**Tests.** Add these to internal/sem/provider_test.go, next to the `TestJulia*` tests (~14671):

1. Exact expected signature strings for these Julia forms:
   - long-form functions
   - functions with a `::T` return type
   - functions with a `where` clause
   - qualified `Base.show`
   - short-form functions
   - macros
   - plain, mutable and parametric structs with `<:`
   - abstract types
   - modules
2. No DATA_FLOWS relation with a `module` symbol at either end. Cover both a Julia module (members with `return f(x)` and an assigned-return) and a Ruby module (`def self.a; return b(); end`). The members' own DATA_FLOWS edges must still be emitted.
3. No USES_TYPE from a function to a type named only in its body. The parameter-type and return-type USES_TYPE and PARAM_TYPE edges must still appear, and so must CONSTRUCTS `bump! -> Counter`.
4. Diff classification: a body-only edit to a Julia function yields `body_changed`, not `signature_changed`. Find the existing `compareEntities`/analyze tests and follow their setup.

**Goldens and contract tests.**

- Regenerate the julia-r-basic golden using the repo's `-update` flag (see golden_test.go) and confirm only signature fields changed.
- Regenerate any other golden that changes, and explain each change.
- Run `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations`, `TestCapabilityRelationDeclarationsMatchIsolatedExtraction` and the language matrix test. `ooRelationSupport["Julia"]` must NOT change.

**Changelog.** Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under the unreleased 0.5.0 section, next to the existing Julia items.

## Verify before committing

- Run `go test ./internal/sem -run 'Julia|Ruby|Capability|LanguageMatrix|Golden|Analyze|Compare'`, then `mise run test`, and `mise run check` if time allows. Report the actual output, and never claim a pass you didn't run.
- Build an after binary: `go build -o /tmp/eg-after ./cmd/entire-graph`. Rerun the repro with both binaries and show:
  - the before and after signatures
  - that the three module DATA_FLOWS edges and `USES_TYPE bump! -> Counter` are gone
  - that the diff now reports `body_changed` for `Shapes.bump!` and `Shapes`

## Finish with

- The commit hash.
- The test commands you ran and their results.
- A PR title and description, ending with "Fixes #350". Sections:
  - Summary
  - Root cause
  - Changes
  - Before/After repro output
  - Tests
  - Follow-ups: ASYNC_CALLS and the HTTP scan still treat modules as callable

title:	Julia: signatures include the whole body, and module symbols get false DATA_FLOWS edges
state:	OPEN
author:	abhi-singhs (Abhi Singh)
labels:	
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:

--
## Summary

There are two precision bugs here. I reproduced both on `main` at `d35078de` with tree-sitter-julia v0.23.1.

1. **Julia signatures include the whole body.** Every Julia function, macro, struct and module stores its full source text as `signature`. A module's signature is its entire module text.
2. **`module` symbols get false `DATA_FLOWS` edges.** The edges come from `return` statements inside the module's member functions. This is not Julia-specific: a Ruby `module` gets the same edges.

Two follow-on effects:

- `diff`/`commit`/`checkpoint` report a body-only edit to a Julia function as `signature_changed`, on both the function and its enclosing module.
- `USES_TYPE` "type referenced in signature" edges are created from body text.

## Reproduction

`src/Shapes.jl`:

```julia
module Shapes

struct Circle
    radius::Float64
end

mutable struct Counter
    count::Int
end

function area(c::Circle)::Float64
    return pi * c.radius^2
end

function bump!(n)
    k = Counter(n)
    k.count = k.count + 1
    return k
end

function work(x)
    return area(x)
end

end
```

`lib/util.rb`, a Ruby control case for the module leak:

```ruby
module Util
  def self.a
    return b()
  end

  def self.b
    1
  end
end
```

Run these commands after committing both files:

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --worktree --profile full --format ndjson > out.ndjson

jq -r 'select(.record_type=="symbol") | "\(.kind):\(.qualified_name)\t\(.signature)"' out.ndjson
jq -r 'select(.record_type=="relation" and .type=="DATA_FLOWS" and (.to_id|test(":module:"))) | "\(.from_id) -> \(.to_id)  [\(.reason)]"' out.ndjson

# then change only `+ 1` to `+ 2` in bump! and `1` to `2` in Util.b, commit, and:
entire graph diff --repo . --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD --json
```

### Observed

Signatures (Julia; Ruby is correct, e.g. `module Util`, `def self.a`):

```
module:Shapes        module Shapes struct Circle radius::Float64 end mutable struct Counter count::Int end function area(c::Circle)::Float64 return pi * c.radius^2 end function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end function work(x) return area(x) end end
struct:Circle        struct Circle radius::Float64 end
struct:Counter       mutable struct Counter count::Int end
method:Shapes.area   function area(c::Circle)::Float64 return pi * c.radius^2 end
method:Shapes.bump!  function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end
method:Shapes.work   function work(x) return area(x) end
```

`DATA_FLOWS` into module symbols (all `resolution: exact`, confidence 0.75):

```
struct:Counter     -> module:Shapes  [callee return value assigned to local and returned by caller]   (really bump!'s)
method:Shapes.area -> module:Shapes  [callee return value flows into caller return value]            (really work's)
method:Util.b      -> module:Util    [callee return value flows into caller return value]            (really Util.a's)
```

The correct edges `Counter -> Shapes.bump!`, `Shapes.area -> Shapes.work` and `Util.b -> Util.a` are also emitted, so the module edges are duplicates attributed to the wrong symbol.

False `USES_TYPE`. `Counter` appears only in the body of `bump!`; the real relation is the `CONSTRUCTS` edge, which is also emitted:

```
USES_TYPE method:Shapes.bump! -> struct:Counter  [type referenced in signature]
```

`diff` after the body-only edits:

```
{"type":"signature_changed","kind":"method","name":"Shapes.bump!", "old_signature":"function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end", "new_signature":"function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 2 return k end"}
{"type":"signature_changed","kind":"module","name":"Shapes"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"method","name":"Util.b"}      <- Ruby: correct
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"module","name":"Util"}        <- Ruby: correct
```

The existing fixture golden `internal/sem/testdata/fixtures/julia-r-basic.ndjson.golden` also records body-laden signatures, for example `function normalize(values) return scale(values) end`.

### Expected

- Header-only signatures: `module Shapes`, `struct Circle`, `mutable struct Counter`, `function area(c::Circle)::Float64`, `function bump!(n)`, `function work(x)`.
- No `DATA_FLOWS` edge with a `module` symbol as an endpoint.
- No `USES_TYPE bump! -> Counter`.
- `body_changed` for `Shapes.bump!` and `Shapes` in the diff.

## Impact

- **Change review:** `compareEntities` (`internal/sem/analyze.go`) checks `Signature` before `BodyHash`. Every Julia body edit is therefore reported as a signature change, on the function and on its module. This defeats the "signature change with many dependents" risk signal.
- **Type edges:** `usesTypeRelations` matches identifiers anywhere in the signature, so any local type named in a body becomes `USES_TYPE`. Signature parsers such as `parameterVarTypes` (`LastIndex(")")`) and `splitSignatureTypes` also read body text.
- **Data flow / `impact`:** a module's `impact` data-flow section lists flows that belong to its functions. The data-flow pass affects Ruby too.
- **Size:** module signatures copy the whole file into every symbol record and the search index.

## Root cause

1. **Signatures.** `signatureFromNode` (`internal/sem/parser.go`, ~8109) ends the signature at a `body` field or a body-like wrapper child. tree-sitter-julia keeps body statements as direct, unlabeled children (`_block` is hidden) of `function_definition`, `macro_definition`, `struct_definition` and `module_definition`, so nothing is cut. Short-form definitions (`f(x) = expr`, an `assignment`) keep the right-hand side too.

   F# has the same grammar shape and already handles it with `fsharpSignature` (`parser.go`, ~4680), which is applied after entity construction (~6488).
2. **Module data flow.** `forEachRelation` sets `callableSymbol := !typeLikeKind(from.Kind)` (`internal/sem/provider.go`, ~5975). `module` is not type-like, so the DATA_FLOWS pass (~6024 → `returnFlowCalls` in `types.go`) runs over the module's block. That block spans all of the module's members: for Julia it is `exactSymbolSource`, for Ruby it is the module's line span.

   The call scan doesn't leak for Julia, because same-container resolution fails closed. F# has `fsharpModuleInitBlock`, but only for its call scan.

## Proposed fix

- **Signatures:** add `juliaSignature(node, src)` modelled on `fsharpSignature`, and recompute `Fingerprint` the same way. Cut rules:
  - `function`/`macro`: the end of the `signature` child. This keeps `::ReturnType` and `where {…}`.
  - `struct`: the end of `type_head`.
  - `module`: the end of the module name.
  - Short-form definitions: the end of the left-hand side.
- **Data flow:** skip the DATA_FLOWS producer when `from.Kind == "module"`, for all languages. No construct the graph labels `module` can hand a value back to a caller, and modules have no parameters to forward, so every flow this pass finds in a module body belongs to a member function. Top-level returns in Lua, PHP, CommonJS and Ruby/Perl scripts are real, but they belong to `file` symbols, which this pass never sees. Leave `callableSymbol` itself alone: it also gates ASYNC_CALLS and the HTTP scan, which may deserve the same treatment in a follow-up.
- **No re-key:** symbol IDs are `repo:language:path:kind:qualifiedName` and don't include the signature, so `IdentityRevision` stays.
- **Cache versions:** bump `searchSnapshotCacheVersion` and `providerRecordsCacheVersion`. Output changes for unchanged trees, and local builds all share provider version `dev`.
- **Capabilities:** `ooRelationSupport["Julia"]` is unchanged. Julia functions still emit USES_TYPE, PARAM_TYPE and DATA_FLOWS.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact header-only signatures for these Julia forms:
  - long-form functions
  - functions with a `::T` return type
  - functions with a `where` clause
  - qualified `Base.show`
  - short-form definitions
  - macros
  - plain, mutable and parametric structs with `<:`
  - abstract types
  - modules
- [ ] No `DATA_FLOWS` relation has a `module` endpoint (Julia and Ruby), while member-function flows are unchanged.
- [ ] No `USES_TYPE` from a function to a type that appears only in its body. Parameter and return-type `USES_TYPE`/`PARAM_TYPE` edges remain.
- [ ] A body-only edit to a Julia function produces `body_changed` in `diff`.
- [ ] Julia symbol IDs are identical before and after the fix.
- [ ] The `julia-r-basic` golden is regenerated with only signature fields changing. Capability-contract and language-matrix tests pass, and `mise run test` passes.

#!/bin/sh
# Usage: run-repro.sh <entire-graph binary> <output dir>
# Runs the issue #350 repro commands against the two-commit repro repo.
set -eu
BIN=$1
OUT=$2
R=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/a1870155-101a-49bb-a35b-e3e8ed3d1416/scratchpad/repro
mkdir -p "$OUT"

# The snapshot runs on the first commit, as in the issue.
git -C "$R" checkout -q --detach main~1
"$BIN" snapshot --repo "$R" --worktree --profile full --format ndjson > "$OUT/out.ndjson"
git -C "$R" checkout -q main

jq -r 'select(.record_type=="symbol") | "\(.kind):\(.qualified_name)\t\(.signature)"' "$OUT/out.ndjson" > "$OUT/signatures.txt"
jq -r 'select(.record_type=="relation" and .type=="DATA_FLOWS" and (.to_id|test(":module:"))) | "\(.from_id) -> \(.to_id)  [\(.reason)]"' "$OUT/out.ndjson" > "$OUT/module-dataflows.txt"
jq -r 'select(.record_type=="relation" and .type=="DATA_FLOWS" and (.from_id|test(":module:"))) | "\(.from_id) -> \(.to_id)  [\(.reason)]"' "$OUT/out.ndjson" > "$OUT/module-dataflows-from.txt"
jq -r 'select(.record_type=="relation" and .type=="DATA_FLOWS") | "\(.from_id) -> \(.to_id)  [\(.reason)]"' "$OUT/out.ndjson" | sort > "$OUT/all-dataflows.txt"
jq -r 'select(.record_type=="relation" and (.type=="USES_TYPE" or .type=="PARAM_TYPE" or .type=="RETURNS_TYPE" or .type=="CONSTRUCTS")) | "\(.type) \(.from_id) -> \(.to_id)  [\(.reason)]"' "$OUT/out.ndjson" | sort > "$OUT/type-edges.txt"

input.content:
## Summary

Fixes two precision bugs from #350:

1. **Julia signatures now end at the declaration header.** Before this change, every Julia function, macro, struct and module stored its whole definition as `signature`, and a module's signature was the entire module. Now they look like `function area(c::Circle)::Float64`, `struct Circle <: Shape` and `module Shapes`.
2. **`module` symbols no longer get `DATA_FLOWS` edges.** The DATA_FLOWS pass scanned a module's block. That block spans the module's members, so every member's return flow was emitted a second time with the module as the endpoint. This affected Ruby as well as Julia.

Because signatures are now correct, three follow-on effects go away:

- **Diffs:** `diff`/`commit`/`checkpoint` report a Julia body-only edit as `body_changed`, not `signature_changed`.
- **Type edges:** types named only in a body no longer produce `USES_TYPE`.
- **Parameter names:** Julia functions now parse parameter names correctly, so parameter-forwarding `DATA_FLOWS` edges are found. Julia now matches Python on the same program (details below).

## Root cause

- **Signatures.** `signatureFromNode` ends a signature at a `body` field or a body-like wrapper child. tree-sitter-julia keeps body statements as direct, unlabeled children of `function_definition`, `macro_definition`, `struct_definition` and `module_definition`, because its `_block` rule is hidden. A short-form definition is an `assignment`. So nothing was ever cut. F# has the same grammar shape and already handles it with `fsharpSignature`.
  - Signature consumers then read body text. `usesTypeRelations` turned every identifier in a body into a USES_TYPE candidate.
  - `parameterNames` reads from the first `(` to the *last* `)`. That made `function work(x) return area(x) end` parse as a parameter named `x)`.
  - `compareEntities` checks `Signature` before `BodyHash`.
- **Module data flow.** `forEachRelation` sets `callableSymbol := !typeLikeKind(from.Kind)`. `module` isn't type-like, so the DATA_FLOWS pass ran over the module's block: `exactSymbolSource` for Julia, the line span for Ruby.

## Changes

- **`internal/sem/parser.go`.** New `juliaSignature(node, src)`, modelled on `fsharpSignature`. It is applied after entity construction, next to the F# override, and recomputes `Fingerprint`.

  | Node | Cut |
  |---|---|
  | `function_definition`, `macro_definition` | end of the `signature` child, so `::ReturnType` and `where {...}` are kept |
  | `struct_definition` | end of `type_head`, so `mutable`, `{T}` and `<: Super` are kept |
  | `abstract_definition`, `primitive_definition` | the whole header, e.g. `abstract type A <: B end` |
  | `module_definition` (and `baremodule`) | end of the module name |
  | short-form `assignment` | end of the left-hand side, e.g. `f(x)::T`, `f(x) where T` |

  If the expected child is missing, the generic `signatureFromNode` result is kept. None of the Julia-gated extraction cases sets `Signature` itself, and every Julia entity is built in `entityFromNode`.
- **`internal/sem/provider.go`.**
  - The DATA_FLOWS pass now also requires `from.Kind != "module"`, for every language. No construct labelled `module` can hand a value back to a caller, and a module has no parameters to forward.
  - That pass is the only DATA_FLOWS producer. Every call-resolution path requires `callableTargetKind`, which admits function, method or type-like kinds only. So no DATA_FLOWS record can have a module at either end.
  - `callableSymbol` itself is unchanged; see Follow-ups.
  - A comment in `resolveJuliaSameContainerMethodCallTargets` said "a short-form signature includes its RHS", which is no longer true. I reworded it. The first-balanced-paren cut it describes still guards against `::typeof(...)` return annotations.
- **Caches.** Output changes for unchanged trees, and every local build shares provider version `dev`, so both cache versions bump:
  - `searchSnapshotCacheVersion` goes from v25 to v26.
  - `providerRecordsCacheVersion` goes from **v20 to v21**, because #349 already took v20.
  - I verified both bumps are load-bearing; see below.
- **No re-key.** IDs are `repo:language:path:kind:qualifiedName` and exclude the signature, so `IdentityRevision` stays.
  - All Julia symbol IDs are identical before and after: 6/6 on the repro and 6/6 on `internal/sem/testdata`.
  - All 426 symbol IDs across `internal/sem/testdata` are identical.
  - Symbol records differ only in `signature`.
- **Goldens.**
  - **`julia-r-basic`**: only the two Julia `signature` fields change in the symbol records. One new relation is correct: `DATA_FLOWS normalize -> scale` (`caller parameter forwarded into callee argument`, evidence `values -> scale()`). The body-laden signature used to hide that `values` is a parameter. The header counts follow: `stats.relations` 7→8, `completeness.relations.DATA_FLOWS` 1→2. The R symbols are unchanged.
  - **`quality_coverage.json`**: the `DATA_FLOWS` tally goes from 26 to 27, for that edge.
  - **Other goldens**: no other golden changes, and none contains a module-kind symbol.
- **Capabilities.** `ooRelationSupport["Julia"]` is unchanged. The language-matrix Julia fixture still emits `USES_TYPE`, `PARAM_TYPE` and `DATA_FLOWS`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`.** New entry under 0.5.0 → Fixed, next to the existing Julia item.

## Before/After repro output

This is the issue's repro: `src/Shapes.jl` and `lib/util.rb`, two commits, the second a body-only edit. I ran it with a binary built from `main` at 2c2abd09 (before) and from this branch (after).

**Signatures** (Julia; Ruby was already right and is unchanged):

```
before
module:Shapes        module Shapes struct Circle radius::Float64 end mutable struct Counter count::Int end function area(c::Circle)::Float64 return pi * c.radius^2 end function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end function work(x) return area(x) end end
struct:Circle        struct Circle radius::Float64 end
struct:Counter       mutable struct Counter count::Int end
method:Shapes.area   function area(c::Circle)::Float64 return pi * c.radius^2 end
method:Shapes.bump!  function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end
method:Shapes.work   function work(x) return area(x) end

after
module:Shapes        module Shapes
struct:Circle        struct Circle
struct:Counter       mutable struct Counter
method:Shapes.area   function area(c::Circle)::Float64
method:Shapes.bump!  function bump!(n)
method:Shapes.work   function work(x)
```

**`DATA_FLOWS` with a module endpoint:**

```
before
method:Util.b      -> module:Util    [callee return value flows into caller return value]
struct:Counter     -> module:Shapes  [callee return value assigned to local and returned by caller]
method:Shapes.area -> module:Shapes  [callee return value flows into caller return value]

after
(none)
```

**Type edges:**

```
before
CONSTRUCTS method:Shapes.bump! -> struct:Counter  [direct call expression resolved to same-file symbol]
PARAM_TYPE method:Shapes.area  -> struct:Circle   [parameter type referenced in signature]
USES_TYPE  method:Shapes.area  -> struct:Circle   [type referenced in signature]
USES_TYPE  method:Shapes.bump! -> struct:Counter  [type referenced in signature]     <- body-only

after
CONSTRUCTS method:Shapes.bump! -> struct:Counter  [direct call expression resolved to same-file symbol]
PARAM_TYPE method:Shapes.area  -> struct:Circle   [parameter type referenced in signature]
USES_TYPE  method:Shapes.area  -> struct:Circle   [type referenced in signature]
```

**All `DATA_FLOWS` after.** The members' own edges are all still there. The two marked `new` appear because the parameter names now parse:

```
method:Shapes.area  -> method:Shapes.work   [callee return value flows into caller return value]
struct:Counter      -> method:Shapes.bump!  [callee return value assigned to local and returned by caller]
method:Util.b       -> method:Util.a        [callee return value flows into caller return value]
method:Shapes.work  -> method:Shapes.area   [caller parameter forwarded into callee argument]   new
method:Shapes.bump! -> struct:Counter       [caller parameter forwarded into callee argument]   new
```

For comparison, the same program in Python produces exactly these four Julia edge shapes, including both forwarding edges.

**`diff --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD`:**

```
before
{"type":"signature_changed","kind":"module","name":"Shapes","old_signature":"module Shapes struct Circle … k.count + 1 … end","new_signature":"module Shapes struct Circle … k.count + 2 … end"}
{"type":"signature_changed","kind":"method","name":"Shapes.bump!","old_signature":"function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 1 return k end","new_signature":"function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) k.count = k.count + 2 return k end"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"method","name":"Util.b"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"module","name":"Util"}

after
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"module","name":"Shapes"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"method","name":"Shapes.bump!"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"method","name":"Util.b"}
{"type":"body_changed","kind":"module","name":"Util"}
```

**The cache bumps matter.** I ran each binary in turn against one shared cache, using a scratch `HOME`, on the repro's committed tree. The probe is the signature of `Shapes.bump!`:

| Run | Snapshot (records cache) | `query --head` (search cache) |
|---|---|---|
| before binary (writes the cache) | `function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) … end` | `function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) … end` |
| this fix *without* the bumps | `function bump!(n) k = Counter(n) … end` (stale hit) | same, stale |
| this fix with the bumps | `function bump!(n)` | `function bump!(n)`, in a new `search-snapshot-v26-4` directory |

## Tests

New tests in `internal/sem/provider_test.go`, next to the `TestJulia*` tests:

- **`TestJuliaSignaturesStopAtDeclarationHeader`** pins exact signatures for 20 forms:
  - long-form functions, including one whose arguments span two lines
  - `::T` return types
  - `where {T<:Real}` and `::T where T`
  - `Base.show`
  - short forms with `::T` and `where`
  - macros
  - plain, mutable and parametric structs with `<:`
  - abstract and primitive types
  - `module` and `baremodule`
- **`TestJuliaAndRubyModulesEmitNoDataFlows`** checks that no DATA_FLOWS record has a module at either end, for a Julia module (`return f(x)` plus an assigned return) and a Ruby module (`def self.a; return b(); end`). The members' own edges are still required.
- **`TestJuliaUsesTypeReadsOnlyTheSignature`** checks that there is no `USES_TYPE bump! -> Counter`. It also requires the param-type `USES_TYPE`/`PARAM_TYPE`, the return-type `USES_TYPE`, and `CONSTRUCTS bump! -> Counter`.
- **`TestJuliaBodyOnlyEditIsBodyChanged`** checks that `compareEntities` on parsed before/after sources reports `body_changed` for `Shapes.bump!`, the short-form `Shapes.double` and `Shapes`, and nothing else.

All four fail on `main` with exactly the issue's symptoms, and pass with this change.

Commands run:

- `go test ./internal/sem -run 'Julia|Ruby|Capability|LanguageMatrix|Golden|Analyze|Compare'`: ok, 126 top-level tests passed, 0 failed.
- `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations`, `TestCapabilityRelationDeclarationsMatchIsolatedExtraction`, `TestLanguageExtractionMatrix`, `TestLanguageMatrixCoversEverySemanticLanguage` and `TestLanguageMatrixCallsGapsAreExactlyAsAudited`: pass.
- `mise run test`: all packages ok.
- `mise run check`: CHECK_RESULT

## Follow-ups

`callableSymbol` is still true for modules. It also gates two scans that read the same member-spanning block:

- **The HTTP scan (`fileNeedsHTTPScan && callableSymbol`).** This one is observable on this branch. A Ruby `module Client` whose `def self.users` calls `HTTP.get("/users")` gets `HTTP_CALLS module:Client -> /users` next to the method's own edge.
- **ASYNC_CALLS (`needsAsyncCalls && callableSymbol`).** Same gate, same block. I didn't reproduce an instance here.

Both probably want the same `from.Kind != "module"` treatment, with their own tests and goldens. I left them out of this PR on purpose.

Cut Julia signatures at the header and stop module DATA_FLOWS

tree-sitter-julia keeps body statements as direct, unlabeled children of
function, macro, struct and module definitions, and a short-form
definition is an assignment, so signatureFromNode never found a body
boundary: every Julia signature carried the whole definition, and a
module's carried every member. compareEntities checks the signature
first, so a Julia body edit read as signature_changed on the function and
again on its module; USES_TYPE turned types named in a body into edges;
and parameterNames parsed the body into the parameter list, hiding
parameter-forwarding flows.

juliaSignature now ends the signature at the signature child (functions
and macros, keeping ::ReturnType and where clauses), at type_head
(structs), at the module name, or at the left-hand side of a short-form
definition, keeps abstract/primitive headers whole, and leaves the
generic signature in place when the child is missing. It is applied
after entity construction like the F# override and recomputes the
fingerprint.

The DATA_FLOWS pass also scanned module symbols, whose block spans their
members, so each member's return flows were emitted again with the
module as the endpoint, in Julia and Ruby alike. It now skips modules in
every language; call resolution never yields a module target, so no
DATA_FLOWS record has a module at either end. callableSymbol is
unchanged and still gates ASYNC_CALLS and the HTTP scan.

Symbol IDs exclude the signature, so IdentityRevision stays. Output
changes for unchanged trees and local builds share provider version
"dev", so the caches move to search-snapshot-v26 and provider-records-v21
(v20 was taken by the records spool).

The julia-r-basic golden changes in its Julia signature fields and gains
one correct DATA_FLOWS edge, normalize -> scale: normalize forwards its
parameter, which the body-laden signature used to hide.
